name: Jack Clark
milestone_by_age_26: No material founder/engineer milestone by age 26 found. Technology journalism at The Register (~2010–2014, ages ~22–26) and Bloomberg (from 2014) preceded OpenAI policy work and Anthropic co-founding in 2021 (~age 33).
early_history_summary: Born in Brighton, England; studied English literature and creative writing. Early career as a London tech copywriter then distributed-systems and AI-adjacent reporter at The Register before moving to Bloomberg in San Francisco; later OpenAI policy director and Anthropic co-founder/head of policy.
evidence_summary: Forbes lists Clark as age 37 with Anthropic co-founding in 2021; longtermwiki and profiles give birth year ~1988. Pre-26 record is tech journalism, not a dated material product, research, or company milestone. Import AI, OpenAI policy leadership, and Anthropic founding all land after age 26.

name: Erik Broes
milestone_by_age_26: No reliably dated material milestone by age 26 found. Known as Mojang Minecraft engineer (Grum) after playing Minecraft from ~2010 and being hired for mod API/server work (~2011–2012); birth year not solidly verified in primary sources (secondary sites claim Dec 2, 1980, which would place Mojang hire near age 30–32).
early_history_summary: Dutch software engineer known as Grum; active Minecraft player/mod community contributor who joined Mojang Studios to work on official modding API and server, later broader game development duties from about August 2012.
evidence_summary: Minecraft Wiki and community sources document Mojang employment and December 2 birthday but not a verified birth year from primary biographical sources. Cannot place a material dated milestone at age ≤26 with two-source confidence; famous-birthdays-style 1980 claims are untrusted alone and would make Mojang work post-26.

name: Jacob Appelbaum
category: Computer security researcher, Tor developer, journalist
milestone_by_age_26: In 2008 (age 25), co-authored the USENIX Security Best Student Paper cold-boot attack paper (“Lest We Remember”) with Halderman, Felten, and others, also winning a Pwnie Award for Most Innovative Research.
early_history_summary: Born April 1, 1983 into a highly unstable family; left formal schooling early and taught himself systems and security. Spoke at Chaos Communication Congress in 2005–2006, collaborated on high-impact crypto/security research by 2008 (cold boot; MD5 collision work), and became a core Tor Project developer and later WikiLeaks/Snowden-era journalist.
family_context_summary: Described a chaotic childhood: mother with severe mental illness, foster/children’s home placement, custody with an indigent father struggling with addiction; later stated programming and the internet were lifelines.
parent_family_domain_summary: No parental domain advantage in security/crypto; path was self-directed after early adversity.
primary_early_advantage_tags: adversity catalyst, self-taught security, hacker conferences, Princeton/EFF cold-boot collaborators, Tor/anonymity community
evidence_summary: Birth date and cold-boot co-authorship are documented on Wikipedia and USENIX/Pwnie records (July 2008 symposium, age 25). Pre-26 path shows deep systems/security reps, CCC talks, and elite research collaborators rather than family capital or elite undergrad pipelines. Later Tor spokesperson role, Snowden journalism, and 2016 misconduct fallout define a tier-3 notability with high leverage confidence on the technical milestone itself.
starting_point: Born 1983 in the U.S. into a highly unstable household; spent parts of childhood in a children’s home and later with an indigent father before self-directed tech education.
current_position: Lives in Berlin as an independent security researcher/journalist; earned a PhD from Eindhoven (2022); subject of a 2024 documentary on his career and allegations; no longer affiliated with Tor.

trajectory.event: Gave Chaos Communication Congress talks on disaster-tech media and disk encryption, entering European hacker research circuits.
Co-authored cold-boot attack paper that won USENIX Security Best Student Paper and a Pwnie Award for innovative research.
Became a high-profile WikiLeaks-associated security figure and stood in for Assange at U.S. hacker conferences.
Among journalists with direct Snowden document access; Der Spiegel reporting on NSA surveillance of allies.
Shared Henri Nannen Prize for investigative reporting on U.S. surveillance of Angela Merkel.
Left Tor Project amid sexual misconduct allegations later supported by Tor’s external investigation; denied allegations.
Completed PhD at Eindhoven University of Technology on communication under pervasive surveillance.

name: Edward G. Amoroso
category: Cybersecurity executive, AT&T CISO, TAG Cyber founder
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently notable milestone by age 26 found. Physics B.S. 1983 (~21), early Singer-Kearfott/Space Shuttle software ~1984, joined Bell Labs ~1985 (~23–24); Ph.D. 1991, major books/CISO role and TAG Cyber founding came later.
early_history_summary: Born Neptune Township, New Jersey (1961); Christian Brothers Academy then Dickinson College physics; M.S./Ph.D. Stevens Institute of Technology; long AT&T/Bell Labs career culminating as first AT&T CISO (2005), later TAG Cyber founder and NYU cybersecurity professor.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a large Italian-American family in Neptune, New Jersey; detailed wealth/domain advantage not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as cybersecurity/domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Infosecurity profile place birth Dec 3, 1961 and early AT&T path, but independently famous milestones (Amoroso threat-tree textbook 1994, CISO 2005, TAG Cyber) are after age 26. Pre-26 record is solid junior engineering, not a breakout dated achievement.

name: Maria-Florina Balcan
milestone_by_age_26: No dated material research breakout verifiably by age 26 found. University of Bucharest B.S. 2000 and M.S. 2002, CMU Ph.D. 2008 under Avrim Blum; major recognition (Sloan 2014, ACM Grace Murray Hopper 2019, ACM Fellow 2023) arrived well after typical age-26 window.
early_history_summary: Romanian-trained mathematician/computer scientist; summa cum laude double major at University of Bucharest, then CMU Ph.D. (2008) on theoretical frameworks for machine learning; postdoc Microsoft Research New England; faculty at Georgia Tech then tenured CMU professor.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and ACM materials confirm degrees and later awards but omit birth year. Ph.D. in 2008 and field-defining recognition years later do not establish a specific ≤26 milestone with two-source dating; early Ph.D. course papers alone do not clear the material-breakout bar without age confirmation.

name: Thomas Knoll
milestone_by_age_26: Photoshop-origin work began fall 1987 when Knoll was about 27 (born 1960); Display→ImagePro→Photoshop licensing to Adobe in 1988 and Photoshop 1.0 (1990) were after age 26. U-M B.S. 1982 / M.S.E. 1984 are education, not the material product milestone.
early_history_summary: Born and raised Ann Arbor, Michigan; son of U-M nuclear engineering professor Glenn Knoll; B.S. 1982 and M.S.E. 1984 at Michigan, then Ph.D. studies in computer vision. In 1987 began Display image routines on a Macintosh Plus; with brother John commercialized as Photoshop with Adobe.
family_context_summary: Father Glenn Knoll was a University of Michigan nuclear engineering professor and amateur photographer; family darkroom and early home computers (Apple II, later Mac).
parent_family_domain_summary: Strong photography/engineering household culture via father’s hobbies and academic environment; not a commercial software firm inheritance.
evidence_summary: Multiple histories (U-M Record, Computer History Museum, Adobe retrospectives) place Display/Photoshop start in 1987 at age ~27 given 1960 birth year. Strict age≤26 rule excludes Photoshop as the qualifying milestone despite enormous later impact and Academy Sci-Tech Award (2019).

name: Rainer Grimm
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Worked as software architect/team lead/instructor from ~1999; first widely noted C++11 book ~2011 and Modernes C++ blogging/teaching career in the 2010s; died October 6, 2025. Birth year not documented; career timing implies post-26 breakout.
early_history_summary: German C++ educator and author of multiple modern C++ books; long industry career from 1999, independent instructor from mid-2010s, active ISO C++ community presence via modernescpp.com until death from ALS-related complications in 2025.
evidence_summary: Meeting C++, modernescpp.com, and community obituaries confirm architect-from-1999 path and 2025 death; no dated ≤26 achievement or birth year in reviewed sources.

name: Byju Raveendran
milestone_by_age_26: No company-scale material milestone by age 26. Born Jan 5, 1980; informal CAT tutoring after helping friends ~2003 (age ~23) and high CAT percentiles, but Byju's Classes founded 2007 (age 27) and Think & Learn / BYJU'S app era 2011–2015 (ages 31–35).
early_history_summary: Born Azhikode, Kerala to teacher parents; engineering degree Government College of Engineering Kannur; brief shipping-company job; built reputation tutoring CAT, then founded Byju's Classes (2007) and later India's largest edtech platform before a severe corporate collapse and governance crises in the 2020s.
family_context_summary: Parents Raveendran and Shobhanavalli were physics and mathematics teachers in Kerala; middle-class teaching household.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents taught math/physics; domain-adjacent education exposure without a documented business platform.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Economic Times list birth 5 Jan 1980; Hindustan Times/CNBC place formal Byju's Classes founding in 2007 at age 27. Early tutoring is real but not treated as the independently material company milestone for strict ≤26 eligibility.

name: Jon Callas
milestone_by_age_26: No dated material crypto/product milestone by age 26 found. University of Maryland B.Sc. math 1977–1980; Century Computing then Digital Equipment principal engineer 1981–1993; OpenPGP/PGP Corporation/Silent Circle achievements are 1990s–2010s. Birth year not published; timeline implies DEC-era work spans past 26 without a singular breakout before then.
early_history_summary: American cryptographer and security engineer; long DEC career, Apple security work, chief scientist roles at original PGP Inc. and co-founder/CTO of PGP Corporation and Silent Circle; later ACLU/EFF public-interest technology roles and SRI.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and career bios document UMD study 1977–1980 and continuous industry security leadership, but lack birth year and a clearly dated ≤26 milestone comparable to OpenPGP authorship or company founding.

name: Rewon Child
milestone_by_age_26: Birth year not documented; cannot verify age at Sparse Transformer (2019), GPT-2 (2019), or GPT-3 (2020) co-authorship. Career trail (Enlitic 2015–16, Baidu 2016–17, OpenAI 2018–20) is material but undated against age ≤26.
early_history_summary: ML researcher who worked medical imaging at Enlitic, speech at Baidu’s Andrew Ng lab, then OpenAI algorithms (Sparse Transformer; GPT-2/3 co-author), later Google Brain, founding team at Inflection AI, and Microsoft AI technical staff.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; personal site notes half-Japanese heritage.
evidence_summary: Personal site and OpenAI/arXiv pages establish high-impact LLM contributions from 2019, but without a sourced birth year eligibility under strict age≤26 cannot be confirmed—mark ineligible rather than force a milestone.

name: Stanley Tang
milestone_by_age_26: In 2013 at about age 20–21, co-founded Palo Alto Delivery / DoorDash with Tony Xu, Andy Fang, and Evan Moore while a Stanford CS student; company later became a major public on-demand delivery platform.
early_history_summary: Born 1992 in Sendai, Japan; raised in Hong Kong (King George V School). Early computing from childhood; published Amazon-bestselling entrepreneur interviews book eMillions around age 15; Stanford CS (grad 2014) with brief Facebook internship; co-founded DoorDash in 2013 and later led product and DoorDash Labs.
family_context_summary: Hong Kong upbringing after Japan birth; specific parental occupations and wealth not detailed in reviewed sources; early international schooling and U.S. university path imply middle/upper resources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as food-delivery or venture-domain family apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford CS, cofounder team, Bay Area on-demand wave, early teen internet ventures, book platform, DoorDash founding
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Forbes, DoorDash IR, and SCMP corroborate 1992 birth, 2013 founding while a Stanford student (~21), and teen eMillions bestseller. Complementary cofounders, Stanford ecosystem, and structural on-demand delivery wave are clear; family domain inheritance is not. IPO made him a billionaire; success_tier 2 for dominant category company builder rather than global cultural icon.
starting_point: Born 1992 in Sendai, Japan; raised in Hong Kong with early access to computing and international schooling before Stanford.
current_position: Co-founder and Head of DoorDash Labs / director at DoorDash; Forbes billionaire (~$1B+ range in recent profiles); married Gloria Zhu (2023).

trajectory.event: Published eMillions interviews with internet entrepreneurs; became an Amazon bestselling teen author in Hong Kong.
Brief software engineering internship at Facebook while studying computer science at Stanford.
Co-founded Palo Alto Delivery / DoorDash with Stanford peers to deliver from local restaurants.
Graduated Stanford BS Computer Science; continued as DoorDash product leader.
Became Head of DoorDash Labs focusing on robotics and last-mile automation.
DoorDash IPO made Tang and co-founders billionaires on paper.
Married Gloria Zhu; continued board/Labs leadership at public DoorDash.

name: Hui Lei
category: Cloud/systems software executive, IBM Distinguished Engineer
milestone_by_age_26: No dated material milestone by age 26 found. B.S. Sun Yat-sen, M.S. NYU, Ph.D. Columbia (1998 thesis on file-reference correlations); long IBM Research career (Watson Health Cloud CTO, Distinguished Engineer) and later Meta engineering leadership—recognition is mid-career, not ≤26.
early_history_summary: Chinese-American computer scientist specializing in distributed systems, cloud, and mobile computing; Columbia Ph.D. 1998; decades at IBM including Distinguished Engineer and Watson Health Cloud CTO; later Futurewei VP and Meta Director of Engineering; IEEE Fellow.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and IEEE Computer Society profiles document Ph.D. 1998 and senior IBM/Meta roles but no birth year or ≤26 breakout achievement with independent dating.
